newsitem.title: TURKEY: Conservatives threaten to quit Turkey coalition.
newsitem.headline: Conservatives threaten to quit Turkey coalition.

text.p: The conservative partner in Turkey's shaky coalition decided late on Wednesday to withdraw from the government unless its leader Tansu Ciller is made prime minister by June 18, a senior party official said.

The True Path Party "has unanimously decided to withdraw from the government if Ciller is not made prime minister unconditionally," deputy party chairman Mehmet Gozlukaya was quoted as saying by the state-run Anatolia news agency.
"Unless the premiership is handed over to Tansu Ciller by June 18, the party's decision-making body will meet to decide to withdraw from the government," he said.

Earlier in the day Ciller had announced that there would be a change of government within days to resolve a row with the secular military that has brought the Islamist-led coalition to the breaking point.
"A change of government is expected in the coming days," Ciller told deputies from her party in parliament.

Ciller and Islamist Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan announced on June 1 that they would seek early elections to overcome a growing dispute with the secular establishment over demands for a crackdown on religious activism.
Under the plan, Erbakan would hand over power to Ciller who would head a caretaker government to prepare for elections.

Temel Karamollaoglu, a deputy chairman of the senior coalition partner Welfare Party, said earlier that elections were expected to take place in October and a parliamentary decision to go for early elections would be taken this month.

But opposition parties and analysts said early elections before an upgrade of electoral rolls, which should be carried out after October 26 by law, were not possible and suggested they take place in March, 1998.
Officials from the High Election Board have said they needed at least six to eight months from October to complete the upgrade of the rolls.
